name: Fogg Behavior Model
description: A behaviour happens when motivation, ability and a prompt (trigger) coincide at the same moment; if any is missing the behaviour does not occur. Used as a checklist for analysing why a target behaviour is not happening and what to change.
design_relevance_note: A diagnostic lens for onboarding and engagement design: ask whether users lack motivation, ability (the action is too hard) or a well-timed prompt, and fix the weakest of the three rather than adding more persuasion.
myth_risk_note: The model is often presented as an established law of behaviour. It is a proposed framework with one narrow supporting study found.
prevalence_note: Widely taught in UX and product-design circles; the usual route to it is Fogg's own materials, not independent evidence.

findings.description: In a two-round panel survey of 617 married men in urban Pakistan, condom use related to motivation, ability and a prompt as the Fogg Behavior Model hypothesises: after adjustment, men with high motivation and high ability had 34 times the odds of condom use of men with low motivation and low ability, and the association between the prompt and condom use operated through increased motivation and ability. Observational and single-setting.
findings.effect_size: adjusted odds ratio ~34 (high vs low motivation and ability); n = 617, two panel rounds
findings.source_title: Use of the Fogg Behavior Model to Assess the Impact of a Social Marketing Campaign on Condom Use in Pakistan
